memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is wicked. Both he and they must be burned in the fire, so that no wickedness will be among you. If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he is to be put to death, and you must kill the animal. If a woman approaches an animal to have sexual relations with it, kill both the woman and the animal. They are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.'" - Lev 20:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses are hard to read, and there is no way to make them comfortable.

What we can see is the phrase in verse 14: so that no wickedness will be among you. God's stated concern is the community. He is not merely punishing individuals; He is preventing something from taking root and spreading.

That principle survives into the New Testament, even though the penalties do not. When the Corinthian church tolerated serious sexual sin among its members, Paul was appalled — not only at the sin but at their complacency about it. His instruction was not execution but removal from fellowship, and he used a striking image: don't you know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough? (1 Cor 5:6).

A little yeast. Sin that is tolerated does not stay contained. It changes the character of the whole community.

That is why churches need loving, careful discipline — not to punish, but to protect. And Paul's stated goal was always restoration of the person, not their destruction (2 Cor 2:6-8).

The severity here reflects how seriously God takes what damages a people. The method has changed entirely under the new covenant. The seriousness has not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to tolerate what should be addressed?
2. How can a church confront sin while genuinely aiming at restoration?
3. What "little yeast" might be working quietly in your own life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You care about the health of Your people. Give our churches courage to address what harms us and grace to always aim at restoration. Amen.
